Vineet Shaky S/o Sh.Keshav Shaky (hereinafter referred as claimant) on account of injuries sustained by him in a road accident which took place on 29.09.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of Truck bearing Registration No. RJ 11 GA 0795 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) which was being driven by Sh. Amir (hereinafter referred as driver/R1), owned by Sh. Tamjid Khan (hereinafter referred as owner/ R2) and insured with M/s The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. (hereinafter referred as insurance company/R3). 2. In the accident in question, claimant sustained grievous injuries while two other persons died at the spot. Accordingly, three separate Claim Petitions were filed before this Tribunal. Present Claim Petition is relating to injuries sustained by the claimant in such alleged road accident. MACT No .348/2018 Vineet Shaky vs. Amir Page N 3. Briefly, the facts, as stated in the Claim Petition, are that on 29.09.2017 at about 12.00 (midnight) claimant alongwith other passengers was traveling in Car (i- 10) bearing Registration No. HR 13K 3831 (hereinafter called the accidental vehicle) which was being driven by Sh. Ashu Chauhan and when they reached on Dankor/Sikandrabad Road, Crown Plaza, PS Dankor, Gautam Budh Nagar, UP (hereinafter called the spot of accident), their car rammed in stationed offending vehicle covered with black Tripal/cover and abandoned on the road without any sign, indicator or reflector, as result of which driver of accidental vehicle Sh. Ashu Chauhan and Sh.Sunil Kumar (who was sitting beside the driver seat) died at the spot, while claimant (who was sitting on the rear seat of the said car) sustained grievous injuries. It is stated that claimant was rushed to Yatharth Hospital, Greater Noida and then remained hospitalised in Beg Hospital and Fahmy Maternity Centre Bareilly for treatment. It is alleged that accident occurred due to unattended offending vehicle parked in the middle of the road. Further, as per record, FIR No. 0586/2017 was registered at PS Dankor, District Gautam Budh Nagar, UP. After completion of investigation, respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted for commission of offence punishable under Section 279/338/304A IPC. 4. It is further asserted that claimant was employed as Salesman with Paramount Road Safety Equipment Pvt. Ltd., Shop No. 20, 26 & 27, DLF. Tower-B, Jasola, Delhi and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month. It is further asserted that claimant sustained grievous injuries in accident due to which he has not been able to attend the office and suffered huge financial loss. It is further stated that the offending vehicle was in immediate control of respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2, while it was MACT No .348/2018 Vineet Shaky vs. Amir Page No. 3 of 27 insured with respondent no.3 and hence, all respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. Hence, the present petition has been filed with a request to pass an Award in the sum of Rs.20,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 12% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization in favour of the claimant and against the respondents. 5. Common written statement was filed by respondent Nos. 1 and 2, wherein it is stated that accident took place on account of negligent driving of claimant. It is also stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured and that the driver was holding a valid driving license and as such, liability, if any, in terms of claim/compensation is upon the insurance company. Vineet Shaky vs Amir on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27361723/ 2 6. Respondent No.3 in the written statement/reply filed, asserted that accident took place due to sole carelessness and negligence of the driver of accidental vehicle as he was not cautious with the traffic moving ahead and ended up ramming into a stationary truck. It is contended that accident is attributed to contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the said accidental vehicle citing the manner of accident. 8. During the course of proceedings, upon moving an application, claimant was referred to Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya Hospita, GNCTD, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi for getting the physical disability assessed. Report from the said hospital was received with 'zero' percent disability. 9. Thereafter, matter was proceeded further for Petitioner Evidence. Claimant appeared as PW1 and tendered his evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. Claimant relied upon his Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1, Medical Treatment bills Ex.PW1/2 (colly), Medical Treatment Record and Discharge Summary Ex.PW1/3, Payment Receipts Ex.PW1/4 (colly) and Salary-cum-Employment Certificate Ex.PW1/5. He was put to cross-examination by counsel for insurance company, however, on one appeared on behalf of R-1 & R-2 to cross-examine him. 10. PW2 Sh. Nitin Kumar Saxena, Manager of M/s Paramount Road Safety Equipment Pvt. Ltd. was also examined by claimant, who proved his Authority Letter Ex.PW2/1, Appointment Letter of claimant as Ex.PW2/2, Salary Slips from April 2016 to September 2017 as Ex.PW2/3 (18 pages), Salary Payment Record as Ex.PW2/4 and Certificate under Section 65-B of Evidence Act with respect to computer generated record as Ex.PW2/5. 11. Petitioner's evidence was closed vide order dated 09.09.2022. Matter was then fixed for Respondents Evidence, however, no witness was examined on behalf of MACT No .348/2018 Vineet Shaky vs. Amir Page No. 5 of 27 Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 while insurance company/Respondent No. 3 examined Ms.Lalita Anand as R3W1, who tendered her evidentiary affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 and relied upon documents Ex.R3W1/A to R3W1/E. Thereafter, respondents evidence was closed vide order dated 01.08.2023. Vineet Shaky vs Amir on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27361723/ 3 12. 13. Ld. counsel for claimant contended that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle as he abandoned the offending vehicle on the road and that too, covered with black Tripal without any indicator or reflector. He also asserted that claimant sustained serious injuries due to accident and had to incur heavy expenses on his treatment and also suffered income/financial loss. 14. No one has appeared on behalf of Respondent nos. 1 and 2 to argue on their behalf.
